criteria.name: Introduction — Identifies ethical issues and broad links to engineering design; discusses the context of ethical issues in engineering organisations; identifies relevant stakeholders when considering the ethical issues.
criteria.reasoning: Several ethical issues (public safety, data loss, professional integrity, reputation) identified and linked to design. Demonstrates both engineering organisation context (competitive market, six-month cycle) and broad stakeholder map, meeting Excellent descriptor.

evidence.quote: The relevant stakeholders in this scenario include Rachel, Rachel’s company, the chip contract company, the government health department, and the many people

criteria.name: Balanced Discussion — Discusses objective arguments for and against decisions on the ethical issues; draws a conclusion on how stakeholders should make decisions about the issues.
criteria.reasoning: Presents objective for/against arguments with depth (competitive advantage, revenue, job security vs harm, trust, legal costs). Draws stakeholder-specific conclusions, satisfying Excellent requiring multiple stakeholders.

criteria.name: Report Structure, Format and Language — The report includes appropriate sections serving their functions (abstract, introduction, body, and conclusion); maps, figures, tables, and visual elements are correctly used to support discussion; writing is grammatically correct, fluent, concise, easy to read and understand, and uses appropriate word choice; references are well-structured and appropriate, supporting the report’s motivations.
criteria.reasoning: Includes abstract, intro, body, conclusion; fluent with few language errors. Uses relevant references but no figures/tables/maps and limited visual elements, matching Good descriptor, not Very Good which requires several visual types competently.

technical_issues.where: DICUSSION: To Ship or Not to Ship
technical_issues.issue: Conflates Apple consumer demand strategy with safety-critical server QA; analogy weak for safety justification. Some referencing formatting errors from OCR but substantive claims okay.

overall: Solid ethics analysis with balanced arguments, relevant stakeholders, and external cases supporting not shipping. Professional code applied well. Structure clear but lacks visual elements and deeper quantification of risk tradeoff.

feedback.summary: You produced a solid, balanced ethics analysis with clear stakeholder mapping and strong use of external cases. Your strengths are in Introduction and Discussion sections, with well-structured arguments leading to a justified recommendation not to ship. To improve, add differentiated stakeholder decision guidance, deepen quantitative risk evidence, and include visual elements to support your argument.
next_steps: To move C3 from Very good to Excellent, add a stakeholder-differentiated decision matrix in The Most Ethical Path showing distinct impacts/actions for Rachel, company, chip vendor, regulator, and end-users.

To move C4 to Excellent, quantify the trade-off in Discussion: estimate failure probability, patient safety impact, and recall/legal costs alongside your qualitative cases like NHS HSSIB and Volkswagen.
To move C5 to Very good, add 2-3 visual elements: e.g., stakeholder map in Introduction and a pros/cons table in Discussion, and ensure consistent reference formatting.

criteria.C1: You excelled at identifying several ethical issues (public safety, data loss, professional integrity) and linking them to engineering design. Your Introduction clearly shows organisational context (competitive six-month cycle) and a broad stakeholder list including the health department and public.
criteria.C2: You provided objective, in-depth for/against arguments in DICUSSION: To Ship or Not to Ship — competitive advantage and job security versus harm, trust, and legal costs — and drew conclusions for multiple stakeholders, meeting Excellent.
criteria.C3: Your body follows a logical structure linking Discussion arguments to The Most Ethical Path and Conclusion. To reach Excellent, demonstrate systematic understanding for all stakeholders with distinct reasoning for chip vendor vs regulator vs Rachel, not just company vs public.
criteria.C4: You substantiated well with EACE Code and strong cases (NHS HSSIB deaths, Volkswagen scandal, Apple cycle) in The Most Ethical Path. For Excellent, add balanced quantitative evidence (e.g., estimated failure rates, cost figures) alongside qualitative evidence.
criteria.C5: Your report has appropriate sections (Abstract, Introduction, body, Conclusion) and fluent writing using relevant references. For Very good, you need several types of visual elements used competently — e.g., a table or figure — which are currently absent.
